pr_title: Fix testcases to run on duplicated keys
pr_body:
The existing loop pattern did not really run the expected tests on the duplicated keys.

Fixes #23129
pr_comments:
> Another (arguably cleaner?) way of doing this would be to have the shared code as a function, instead of looping.
> Also, I am not sure what the dup test is achieving if the keys are allegedly equal? i.e. what are we really trying to test here?

That the duplicated keys behave the same way as the original keys. The equality test does not actually test for identity. I.e. a public key will match a private key in the equality test.
And no, I am not going to refactor out the loop into separate functions for all these tests, I am sorry but that would be a lot more work.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.2, 3.1 and 3.0 branches. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: Fix the while(dup_pk == NULL) loops in test/evp_pkey_provided_test.c
issue_context.body: The loops which are present in multiple testcases in this file are wrong as they won't repeat the check with the duplicated pkey. They need to be replaced with a for(;;) loop with exit in the middle.
comments:
For more context, here is a pointer to the conversation about the while-loops initiated by Hugo L:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/21875/files#r1318758922

review_comments: I think @slontis noted previously that this could go outside the for loop, or be removed entirely as its assigned below

this has introduce a memory leak above (which has been caught in the CI failure).

`group, group_p, group_a, group_b` are allocated at lines 1691-1694 and then are clobbered in the second loop iteration.

does using `!ret` go against our coding-style?

I don't necessarily think it should be changed (it is used in quite a few places in these files).
Nope, if `ret` is `int` which acts as boolean (which it is), it is fine to use `!ret`.
